glass-dark.notes: roadmap coverage 4 (transparency), 2026-08-18. The DARK half of OPS.glasspair at (0,8,170): unlit rho=0.50 walls sharing one 1-node partition with a furnace-050-walled chamber to the west. Looking -x at that partition from ~3.5 nodes. With an opaque partition this room is EXACTLY black, so the pane material is the only variable and the before-half of the A/B needs no tolerance. NOT a CI arm -- util/claude_glass_probe.py shoots it. Doors plugged before capture (A 3,9,170 with the lit wall; B 9,9,170 with the dark one).

glass-lit.notes: roadmap coverage 4, 2026-08-18. The LIT half of OPS.glasspair: furnace-050 walls, so its interior radiance is the analytic Le/(1-rho) and it is the reference the dark half's reading is quoted against. Looking +x at the partition.

glassfurnace.notes: roadmap coverage 4, 2026-08-18. OPS.glassfurnace at (100,8,170): furnace-050 exactly, plus a one-node slab across the whole interior at z=173. A LOSSLESS dielectric cannot move a sealed furnace's equilibrium, so claude_furnace_check.py must read the same ratio with the slab as air, as the wall node and as glass -- the energy gate for the Fresnel split, and it needs no new referee. Door plugged before capture (103,9,170).

skyfurnace-050.notes: roadmap 1b: open flat rho=0.50 pad (24x24, no walls), fenced yard (fence >=12 nodes from pad centre at (60,8,110), 1 node high). Camera looking down ~45deg so only pad fills frame. Referee (2b): L = rho*L_sky under a uniform test sky. Dark/placeholder until 2b.

sealed-plank-down.notes: THE SEALED-PLANK REFEREE (2026-08-18, John's request: "a fully enclosed house, with a wall of emissive blocks surrounding it entirely... the room should be completely dark, any holes would bleed through"). ONE interior standing position, aiming -Y (85 deg, clear of the pitch clamp). The room is an oak-plank box, wall EXACTLY 1 node thick (the carved relief that leaked, fixed by b945042ee), inside a 1-node air gap inside a shell of claude_bridge:white_lit. Nothing lights the interior, so ANY non-black pixel is a leak and the analytic answer is 0. SIX AIMS AND NOT ONE: John's own observation of the original defect was that it "seems to occur only when looking east" -- a leak is a particular ray through a particular groove pair, so a single fixed vantage can miss it entirely. No door to plug: the room has none, a doorway would pierce all three shells. y = 11 is the teleport aim; the body rests at 10.5 on the plank floor, the same half-node fall every gallery vantage takes.
